text:
Elliot R: Quick thread: debating micro interactions for the new multi-section Create Policy form. Main points: live inline validation vs summary-only, how to show required fields without clutter, and delete/destructive copy. Thoughts? Samir: My take: validate as-you-type for deterministic checks (email format, max length). For missing required fields only show after first submit to avoid yelling at users while typing. Nia: +1. Also recommend minimal inline hints (one line) and only expand to a summary when submit has multiple errors. Summary should be keyboard-focusable and link to fields. Jordan: accessibility nit: always include `aria-required=\"true\"` on required inputs, and ensure `aria-describedby` points to the error text. Example we use: ```
Enter a policy name
``` Elliot R: good. On required markers: asterisk-only is ambiguous for some users. Maybe show a visible "Required" label on top of compact fields and for long forms use a legend stating "Fields marked Required are needed to save". Samir: yep. Also prefer action-first microcopy for errors. Instead of "Name is required" use "Enter a policy name" — testing shows it reduces cognitive load. Nia: Delete modal copy: we have three flavors in the wild. Suggestion: soft delete = "Remove from dashboard"; hard delete = "Permanently delete policy" + explainer line. For bulk or production critical items, require typed confirm of the exact policy slug. For single, the checkbox "I understand this cannot be undone" is fine. Jordan: UX detail: when there are errors after submit, move focus to the summary container (tabindex=-1) and ensure each message links to the field via `href=\"#id\"` so it focuses cleanly. Also the summary should have `aria-live=\"polite\"` and the inline field `role=\"alert\"` when it appears after an interaction. Elliot R: what about visual density? Dense forms mean many asterisks look noisy. Any pattern for reducing clutter? Samir: mark required at the section level where fields are all required, and in mixed sections mark individual fields. That cuts down redundancy. Nia: error visuals must not be color-only. Use icon + text + border and ensure contrast of the message text >= 4.5:1. Jordan: small code snippet for summary focus: ```
3 problems found
``` then list items link to `#field-id`. Elliot R: copy variations for delete modal: concise vs explicit. Concise: "Permanently delete policy" + "This cannot be undone." Explicit: "This will permanently delete the policy 'X' and all attached rules and logs. Type the policy slug to confirm." Which should we default to? Samir: default to explicit for anything tagged production or when user has >50 policies. Concise is OK for casual/local items. Nia: I'll draft both copy sets and include examples for mobile modal truncation. Jordan: I'll push a tiny PR that wires `aria-invalid` and the error-summary focus behavior behind a feature flag so we can test A/B. aria-bot: accessibility checklist: https://intranet.redwood/a11y/checklist (posted) Elliot R: plan: Nia writes copy + examples, Samir prototypes inline vs submit-summary in figma, Jordan does small PR. We'll reconvene after mocks. Samir: timeline: prototypes by tomorrow noon. Nia: copy by EOD. Jordan: PR by Friday. Elliot R: thanks all. if no objections i'll lock this as the working pattern for the next sprint (inline validations for deterministic checks, summary after submit when >2 errors, visible required markers policy-level, typed-confirm for bulk/prod deletes). Samir: no objections. Nia: thumbs up. Jordan: good to go from eng.
